reading: The innocent reading first. Under the exact-match operator the Overview identifies the piece, gives both names of its byline, places it in Pearl and Other Poems as its footnote, and describes its operation as a parody of Kerouac that moves his rules for spontaneous writing into telepathy and mind control. It gives the two authors as figures of experimental literary projects, fictional personas and online literature discussions, and offers two next steps: Kerouac's thirty points, or the background of Lee Sharks and Jack Feist. Its sources are the archive's capture records, the IDP map of the book, a Medium post carrying the book's contents, and the 2014 forum posting of the text. The results page below adds the Hugging Face poetics dataset (pearl/12), an Academia.edu PDF of the book whose contents set the Footnote at page 19, four more of the archive's capture records, and the forum's search page with the thread's tags.
analysis: Quoted, the title resolves to the work, and the work arrives inside the frame the archive has spent the most effort recording as a machine error. The composition's sources explain why: it reads the archive's records of earlier compositions, so the earlier compositions' frame is the frame it finds. What it adds is its own: the forum posting becomes the genre, and the 2014 book becomes a metadata project. Its offered next step is Kerouac's list, and the unquoted address, seated the same day, shows that step taken by the Overview unasked. The organic layer under the panel holds better material than the panel composes from: the forum thread of December 2014 with its tags, and a second state of the book.
